title: Beachfront Fire Island home reduced to rubble by raging caught-on-camera inferno
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A massive blaze wiped out a sprawling, wooden beachfront house on Fire Island Wednesday afternoon, shocking video shows.

The inferno broke out at the vacation home in the Fire Island Pines section of the popular Long Island summer destination shortly before 1:15 p.m., according to officials.

People were reportedly inside the residence when the fire erupted but no injuries have been reported.

Harrowing videos show the property engulfed in roaring flames, but it does not appear the fire spread to neighboring homes.

As firefighters battled the blaze, the roof caved in and collapsed, reducing the multi-story home to a pile of flaming rubble, dramatic video shows.

The boardwalk, which provides access to the island’s picturesque beachfront properties, started to burn during the inferno, according to the Suffolk County Department of Fire.

The extent of damage to nearby homes was not immediately clear Wednesday evening.

Thirteen fire departments responded to the scene and attempted to extinguish the out-of-control flames.

Firefighters managed to get the destructive blaze under control by 4:40 p.m., officials said.

Arson Squad detectives are probing the blaze but don’t believe it’s suspicious, Patch reported.

Sources told WABC a barbecue may have sparked the fire.

The home, built in 1976 by architect Steven Robinson, has been determined to be a total loss by officials.

Robinson described the property as an “ecologically pioneering, year round vacation house,” in an interview with Pines Modern.

“The profile of the house follows the natural forms of the dunes and accommodates an array of climatically responsive strategies. The exterior cedar walls blend into the beach palette,” Robinson said.

The Fire Island Fire District was unable to provide information when contacted by The Post Wednesday evening.
